title: FMEA-GPT Subsystem Taxonomy and Failure-Mechanism Narrative Profiles
purpose: Externalizes engineering taxonomy (ATA chapter mapping, component classification profiles, subsystem/stage naming rules, failure-mechanism narrative templates) that previously lived as hard-coded literals in src/agents/providers/local_synthesizer.py and src/agents/nodes/fmea_builder.py. Python code contains only matching/assembly logic; every engineering statement here carries an explicit provenance status.

status_vocabulary.SOURCE_DERIVED: Statement is taken from (or verbatim-quoted from) a document in the indexed corpus; source/page given.
status_vocabulary.REFERENCE_TAXONOMY: Industry reference numbering (e.g. ATA iSpec 2200 chapters). Used only as a navigation label; the specification itself is NOT in the indexed corpus.
status_vocabulary.UNVERIFIED_ENGINEERING_KNOWLEDGE: General engineering description not established by any indexed source. Displayed with an explicit UNVERIFIED label.
status_vocabulary.DOMAIN_HEURISTIC: Expert rule-of-thumb narrative. Never presented as a requirement; carries SupportLevel.DOMAIN_HEURISTIC.
status_vocabulary.NOT_ESTABLISHED_IN_CORPUS: The indexed corpus contains no data for this item (e.g. inspection intervals, occurrence probability). The system must say so rather than invent a value.

ata_chapters._basis: ATA iSpec 2200 / ATA 100 chapter numbering (commercial specification, not in the indexed corpus). Used as labels only.

default_part_number.note: No default part numbers are fabricated. If the user does not supply a P/N the report shows UNSPECIFIED.

failure_mechanism_profiles_note: Narratives are DOMAIN_HEURISTIC / ENGINEERING_INFERENCE templates. They contain NO inspection intervals, OEM task numbers, 'mandatory' language, rotor speeds or gas temperatures. Severity categories are engineering judgments mapping the postulated end effect to MIL-STD-1629A definitions, not OEM or certification severity determinations. Legacy S/O/D scores are quarantined automotive-style values kept only for backward-compatible exports.
not_established_interval: Not established in indexed corpus - defer to OEM engine/component manual and approved maintenance program

failure_mechanism_profiles.cause: Cyclic micro-slip between blade attachment and disk slot contact surfaces under centrifugal and vibratory loading, producing localized contact stress concentrations.
failure_mechanism_profiles.local_effect: Fretting damage and crack nucleation at the edge of contact on attachment (dovetail / fir-tree) bearing surfaces.
failure_mechanism_profiles.next_effect: Fretting-fatigue crack growth into the attachment under combined steady and alternating stress.
failure_mechanism_profiles.end_effect: Potential blade or attachment separation with secondary damage to downstream hardware.

severity.regulatory_hazard_tier: Potential Hazardous Engine Effect if separation is not contained (assessment per 14 CFR § 33.75 / CS-E 510)
severity.justification: Engineering judgment: worst-case end effect (attachment separation) mapped to MIL-STD-1629A Category I definition. Not an OEM or certification severity determination.

failure_mechanism_profiles.cil_reason: Single-point structural load path at the blade attachment; retained as critical item candidate pending OEM review.

detection.statement: Attachment contact surfaces are generally only accessible at disassembly; NDT of blade roots and disk slots at shop visit is the typical detection means (domain heuristic).

failure_mechanism_profiles.recommended_action: Review OEM attachment inspection requirements and contact-surface condition criteria; consider fretting-fatigue analysis of attachment contact stresses (domain heuristic, not a requirement).

failure_mechanism_profiles.cause: Reduced internal coolant flow or degraded internal heat transfer (e.g. passage blockage or flow-path change), raising local metal temperature.
failure_mechanism_profiles.local_effect: Local metal temperature increase in the affected airfoil region.
failure_mechanism_profiles.next_effect: Accelerated temperature-dependent damage (oxidation, creep, thermal-fatigue) in the overheated region.
failure_mechanism_profiles.end_effect: Premature airfoil distress; potential local burn-through or cracking leading to removal.

severity.regulatory_hazard_tier: Engine effect classification not established in corpus (assessment per 14 CFR § 33.75 / CS-E 510)
severity.justification: Engineering judgment: postulated end effect mapped to MIL-STD-1629A Category II definition. Not an OEM or certification severity determination.

failure_mechanism_profiles.cil_reason: Progressive thermal degradation mechanism; retained for review, not a single-point structural failure.

detection.statement: Borescope inspection for local thermal distress and engine performance trend monitoring are typical detection means (domain heuristic).

failure_mechanism_profiles.recommended_action: Review OEM limits for airfoil thermal distress and cooling-passage condition (domain heuristic, not a requirement).

failure_mechanism_profiles.cause: Cyclic thermal gradients during engine transients combined with mechanical (centrifugal) strain.
failure_mechanism_profiles.local_effect: Crack initiation at regions of high cyclic strain such as cooling-hole edges or airfoil leading/trailing edges.
failure_mechanism_profiles.next_effect: Crack propagation and possible local coating damage and aerodynamic distortion.
failure_mechanism_profiles.end_effect: Engine vibration, potential blade fracture and in-flight shutdown.

severity.regulatory_hazard_tier: Potential Major Engine Effect (assessment per 14 CFR § 33.75(g) / CS-E 510)
severity.justification: Engineering judgment: postulated end effect mapped to MIL-STD-1629A Category II definition. Not an OEM or certification severity determination.

failure_mechanism_profiles.cil_reason: Single-part crack mechanism with potential major engine effect; retained as critical item candidate pending OEM review.

detection.statement: Borescope inspection and NDT (e.g. fluorescent penetrant) at overhaul are typical detection means for airfoil cracking (domain heuristic).

failure_mechanism_profiles.recommended_action: Apply OEM crack inspection criteria and limits (domain heuristic, not a requirement).

failure_mechanism_profiles.cause: Sustained centrifugal tensile stress at high metal temperature.
failure_mechanism_profiles.local_effect: Time-dependent inelastic elongation and microstructural damage accumulation.
failure_mechanism_profiles.next_effect: Radial growth leading to reduced tip clearance and possible tip rub.
failure_mechanism_profiles.end_effect: Performance loss and, if unchecked, stress-rupture fracture.

severity.regulatory_hazard_tier: Engine effect classification not established in corpus (assessment per 14 CFR § 33.75 / CS-E 510)
severity.justification: Engineering judgment: postulated end effect (performance degradation) mapped to MIL-STD-1629A Category III definition. Not an OEM or certification severity determination.

failure_mechanism_profiles.cil_reason: Progressive degradation mechanism typically managed on condition; not retained as single-point failure.

detection.statement: Dimensional checks at shop visit and exhaust-gas-temperature trend monitoring are typical detection means (domain heuristic).

failure_mechanism_profiles.recommended_action: Apply OEM dimensional/elongation limits (domain heuristic, not a requirement).

failure_mechanism_profiles.cause: Impact by ingested or internally generated debris.
failure_mechanism_profiles.local_effect: Leading-edge nick, dent or notch producing a local stress concentration.
failure_mechanism_profiles.next_effect: Earlier high-cycle-fatigue crack initiation from the damage site.
failure_mechanism_profiles.end_effect: Possible blade fracture and secondary damage downstream.

severity.regulatory_hazard_tier: Potential Major Engine Effect (assessment per 14 CFR § 33.75(g) / CS-E 510)
severity.justification: Engineering judgment: postulated end effect mapped to MIL-STD-1629A Category II definition. Not an OEM or certification severity determination.

failure_mechanism_profiles.cil_reason: Damage-initiated crack mechanism; retained as critical item candidate pending OEM review.

detection.statement: Borescope inspection after suspected ingestion events is the typical detection means (domain heuristic).

failure_mechanism_profiles.recommended_action: Apply OEM damage limits and repair criteria (domain heuristic, not a requirement).

failure_mechanism_profiles.cause: Bond-coat oxidation / thermally grown oxide growth and thermal cycling, and environmental (hot corrosion) attack of the coating system.
failure_mechanism_profiles.local_effect: Spallation of the ceramic top coat and loss of protective coating.
failure_mechanism_profiles.next_effect: Increased substrate metal temperature and accelerated substrate oxidation in the exposed area.
failure_mechanism_profiles.end_effect: Reduced airfoil life and premature removal; possible local burn-through.

severity.regulatory_hazard_tier: Engine effect classification not established in corpus (assessment per 14 CFR § 33.75 / CS-E 510)
severity.justification: Engineering judgment: postulated end effect (life reduction) mapped to MIL-STD-1629A Category III definition. Not an OEM or certification severity determination.

failure_mechanism_profiles.cil_reason: Gradual degradation mechanism without abrupt structural failure; not retained as single-point failure.

detection.statement: Borescope inspection for coating loss and thermal discoloration is the typical detection means (domain heuristic).

failure_mechanism_profiles.recommended_action: Apply OEM coating-loss limits (domain heuristic, not a requirement).

failure_mechanism_profiles.cause: Crack propagation to critical size in the airfoil or attachment.
failure_mechanism_profiles.local_effect: Separation of the blade or blade fragment from the rotor.
failure_mechanism_profiles.next_effect: Impact on surrounding casing and downstream stages; rotor imbalance.
failure_mechanism_profiles.end_effect: Potential Hazardous Engine Effect if high-energy debris is not contained (14 CFR § 33.75(g)(2) lists non-containment of high-energy debris).

severity.regulatory_hazard_tier: Hazardous Engine Effect (14 CFR § 33.75(g)(2)) if not contained
severity.justification: Engineering judgment: worst-case end effect mapped to MIL-STD-1629A Category I definition. Not an OEM or certification severity determination.

failure_mechanism_profiles.cil_reason: Single-point failure with potential Category I effect under MIL-STD-1629A / NASA-STD-8729.1A critical-item criteria.

detection.statement: Engine vibration monitoring and NDT of blade attachments/disk slots at shop visit are typical detection means (domain heuristic).

failure_mechanism_profiles.recommended_action: Follow OEM vibration exceedance and attachment inspection procedures (domain heuristic, not a requirement).

failure_mechanism_profiles.cause: Contamination or mechanical binding of internal moving elements, or seal degradation.
failure_mechanism_profiles.local_effect: Sluggish, incomplete or uncommanded travel of the moving element, or internal leakage.
failure_mechanism_profiles.end_effect: Loss of precise control authority requiring redundant/back-up function.

severity.regulatory_hazard_tier: Failure-condition classification not established in corpus (assessment per 14 CFR § 25.1309 / CS-E 50)
severity.justification: Engineering judgment: postulated end effect mapped to MIL-STD-1629A Category II definition. Not an aircraft FHA or certification classification.

failure_mechanism_profiles.cil_reason: Control element failure requiring redundancy verification.

detection.statement: Position-feedback monitoring by the control system and functional checks are typical detection means (domain heuristic).

failure_mechanism_profiles.recommended_action: Apply OEM fluid-contamination and functional-check procedures (domain heuristic, not a requirement).

failure_mechanism_profiles.cause: Operational stress exceeding material capability under cyclic loading.
failure_mechanism_profiles.next_effect: Progressive loss of structural stiffness or function.

severity.justification: Domain heuristic: generic degradation mapped to MIL-STD-1629A Category III definition.

detection.statement: Visual inspection during scheduled maintenance (domain heuristic).

failure_mechanism_profiles.recommended_action: Follow OEM maintenance data (domain heuristic, not a requirement).

severity_definitions.CATEGORY_I: Category I - Catastrophic: A failure which may cause death or weapon system loss.
severity_definitions.CATEGORY_II: Category II - Critical: A failure which may cause severe injury, major property damage, or major system damage which will result in mission loss.
severity_definitions.CATEGORY_III: Category III - Marginal: A failure which may cause minor injury, minor property damage, or minor system damage which will result in delay or loss of availability or mission degradation.
severity_definitions.CATEGORY_IV: Category IV - Minor: A failure not serious enough to cause injury, property damage, or system damage, but which will result in unscheduled maintenance or repair.
